source: W3C WAI Before and After Demonstration (BAD), https://www.w3.org/WAI/demos/bad/ : the four 'before' pages' own numbered barrier annotations (annot_01..NN) and the four repaired 'after' pages' annotations, transcribed on 2 Nov 2026. Titles quoted; descriptions paraphrased.

scope.rule: in_scope is decided by kind (doc 19 §19.1), never by what Parity found: perceptual gaps between what a sighted user sees and what a screen reader announces are in scope; structure, presentation and keyboard barriers are counted and reported, never claimed.

anchors: src: an image file name inside the element's outer HTML; text: normalised equality with the element's visible text or the finding's sighted text; html: a substring of the element's outer HTML; css: a fragment of the element's css path. A label matched by several findings counts once.

rows.description: The site logo, an image of text, has an alt of several sentences describing the artwork instead of the words in it (F30).
The concert teaser photo has no alt attribute at all (F65).
The news headline link looks like a heading, so sighted readers may not recognise it as a link.
A CSS background image carries its only text alternative in title="image", which neither describes it nor reaches most readers (F3, F30).
The link text "Read More..." does not say what the link leads to (F63, F84).
Three story columns are one run of text in the markup, so they read as a single sentence (F1, F2).

rows.w3c: 07: Link with image has empty text alternative
rows.description: The "more" arrow links contain only an image with alt="", so the links have no name (F89); three such links on the page.
rows.note: W3C did not number the repaired 'full story' links on the after page.

rows.w3c: 08: Decorative image without empty text alternative
rows.description: The list bullet images have alt="bullet", noise for a screen reader where an empty alt belongs (F39).

rows.w3c: 09: List not marked up as such
rows.description: "Killer bees" and "Onions" look like a list but are not marked up as one (F2).
The hotline number is an image whose alt is the placeholder "1234 56789" (F20, F30, F71).

rows.w3c: 01: Heading not marked up as such
rows.description: "Heat wave linked to temperatures" is styled as a heading but is a paragraph in the markup (F2).
Body text is set in a serif font, which is harder to read on screen.
The two main text columns need more space between them.

anchor.text: Man Gets Nine Months in Violin Case

rows.description: "Your Shout" belongs to the violin story visually but follows "Tough Wahoonie" in the markup (F1).
A linked photo has alt "picture of Clara F.", which describes the picture and not the link's purpose.
"the way that air conditioning works" is a link with no cue but colour (F73).

anchor.text: the way that air conditioning works

rows.w3c: 07: Emphasized text not marked up as such
rows.description: Italic styling stands in for the em element (F2).

anchor.text: but also hot air that's ducted away to the outside

rows.description: "Return To Sender" is formatted with the font element and the align attribute.
The brain-donations chart has alt="" and no text alternative anywhere, so its figures are lost (F30).
The photo's alt tells a story the picture does not show, information that should be text for everyone (F30).

rows.w3c: 01: Image of text without text alternative used as a heading
rows.description: The "Ticket Offers" heading is an image of text with no alt and no heading markup (F71, F2).

rows.w3c: 02: Table column headings not marked up
rows.description: The concert-dates table shows its headers by colour only, with no th and no caption (F43, F2).

rows.w3c: 03: Using CSS to convey semantic meaning
rows.description: "special deals" is bold by CSS rather than the strong element (F2).

rows.w3c: 04: Image of text with incorrect text alternative
rows.description: The hotline image shows "(1) 269 M-U-S-I-C" but its alt says "music line phone number" (F30).
The price table has no caption and no header cells associated with its data cells.
Header text #41545D on #A9B8BF is below the contrast minimum.

rows.w3c: 07: Acronyms used to indicate seat options are not explained
rows.description: "FS", "RS", "DC" and "ST" are never expanded.

rows.w3c: 08: No semantic markup and text is hard to read
rows.description: The terms are an unmarked heading and list in justified, underlined capitals with tight leading (F88).

rows.w3c: 01: Instructions necessary for form completion are missing
rows.description: Nothing says which fields are required.

anchor.text: This Week's Survey: More city parks - a pain or a gain?

rows.w3c: 02: Radio buttons not grouped within the code
rows.description: The park radio buttons have no fieldset or legend.

anchor.text: Which is your favorite city park?

rows.w3c: 03: Radio button is not associated with its label
rows.description: The park radio buttons are not associated with their visible labels; a screen reader announces each as an unnamed radio button.
The city select has no label and no title, so it is announced without a name.

rows.w3c: 05: Select box not easily usable by keyboard
rows.description: The long city list is ungrouped and sorted by country, which hinders keyboard selection.
The newsletter fields are laid out in a table so labels and inputs are read out of order; W3C notes the fields are also not associated with their labels (F49).
rows.note: A finding on the unlabelled newsletter inputs lands here and is counted as out of scope, not as a hit: the numbered barrier is the sequence.

rows.description: Last week's results use paragraphs where table cells belong, so the figures read in the wrong order (F43, F2).

rows.w3c: 01: Text alternative matches the graphical text
rows.description: The logo's alt is the words in the image.
The teaser photo has a short descriptive alt.

rows.w3c: 03: Links highlighted when they receive focus
rows.description: Headline links change colour on focus and hover.
The decorative photo is an img with alt="".

rows.w3c: 05: Link text indicates the link purpose
rows.description: "Buy Tickets" says where the link goes.

rows.w3c: 06: Using CSS rather than tables for layout
rows.description: Each news item is its own block.
Links are underlined and coloured.
The "Elsewhere" links are a ul.
The bullet is a CSS background, not an img.
The hotline number is text, in digits and letters.
Column and line spacing are increased.
The story title is an h2.
Body text is sans-serif.
"Your Shout" follows its story in the markup too.
The linked photo's alt is "Clara F.'s website".
The link is underlined with sufficient contrast.

anchor.text: the way that air conditioning works

rows.w3c: 07: Emphasized text marked up as such
rows.description: The phrase is an em element.

anchor.text: but also hot air that's ducted away to the outside

rows.description: "Return To Sender" is an h3.
The chart's alt carries its figures.
The photo's alt describes the picture; the story is text beside it.
"Citylights Ticket Offers" is an h1 styled with CSS.

rows.w3c: 02: Table headers have been marked up as such
rows.description: The dates table has th cells with scope and a caption.

rows.w3c: 03: Using structure to convey semantic meaning
rows.description: "special deals" is a strong element.
The hotline number is text, in digits and letters.

rows.w3c: 05: Table data has been properly structured
rows.description: The price table has a caption, a summary and id/headers associations.

rows.w3c: 06: Seat options are spelt out in full
rows.description: "Front Seats", "Rear Seats" and so on replace the acronyms.

rows.w3c: 07: Sufficient color contrast to increase readability
rows.description: Header text is #000000 on #c0c0c0.

rows.w3c: 08: Text is marked up semantically and is easier to read
rows.description: The terms are an h2 and an ordered list.
"Fields are required if not otherwise noted." opens the form.

anchor.text: Fields are required if not otherwise noted.

rows.w3c: 02: Radio buttons are grouped within the code
rows.description: The park radios sit in a fieldset with a legend.

rows.w3c: 03: Radio button is associated with its label
rows.description: Each park radio has a label element.
The city select has title="cities of the world".

rows.w3c: 05: Select box with improved keyboard usability
rows.description: Cities are grouped by letter and sorted by city.
Newsletter labels and inputs are in reading order and associated.

rows.w3c: 07: Table data has been properly structured
rows.description: Last week's results use th and td cells.
